newsitem.title: UK: New drugs keep SmithKline healthy.
newsitem.headline: New drugs keep SmithKline healthy.

text.p: Brimming with confidence, SmithKline Beecham Plc sang the praises of its drug development pipeline Monday, saying it keeps the Anglo-American company in good shape to go it alone in a merging industry.

Strong sales growth for antidepressant Paxil/Seroxat is keeping Chief Executive Jan Leschly happy, while five new products have entered their final development stages and are expected to boost results later this decade.
Another group of products based on genetic research is scheduled to go into its first clinical trials next year, Leschly said in an interview.
"We have a product portfolio which is comparable to the best in the business," he told Reuters.
"Sometimes, I would like to say to analysts: 'Do you realise that we have a pipeline that is just as attractive ... for half the amount of research as others?'"

SmithKline last week pleased investors with a 14 percent rise in 1996 profits to 1.55 billion pounds ($2.52 billion), but some industry analysts expressed slight reservations because Leschly said the strength of the pound might rein back earnings growth in 1997.
He predicted Monday that takeover rumours will continue this year but reiterated there is no need for SmithKline to join the drug industry's consolidation.
"If we will continue to do well and we have double-digit growth, why would we need to merge?" he said.
Meanwhile, a handful of new drugs could each generate 300 million to 500 million pounds ($488 million to $814 million) in annual sales if they pass their final tests, he said.
One of the five new medicines targets rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis and asthma. The other four are intended to fight Alzheimer's disease, type-2 diabetes, migraine and irritable bowel syndrome.
